steps_raw.instruction: Preparation of Gelatin Slide Coating Solution
Scope and Applicability: Preparation of gelatin solution to be used for coating glass microscope slides.
Gelatin powder (Type A, 275 bloom, Fisher G8-500 or equivalent)
Chrome alum, Chromium (III) Potassium Sulfate dodecahydrate (Sigma 243361 or equivalent)
Glass Erlenmeyer flask or beaker (500 ml or appropriate size, as determined by desired yield)
0.3% gelatin solution with chrome alum
Warning: Personal Protective Equipment () should be used at all times while operating this protocol. If you are unsure what you should be using, see your immediate supervisor.
Determine the required volume of gelatin solution.
Determine the correct size glass container to use, to hold solution.
Methodology/Procedures:
Add the required volume of MilliQ water to a glass container according to Table 1.
Table 1: 0.3% Gelatin Solution
Once the water has reached 65C, gently add the gelatin powder (avoid clumps).
Heat the water to 65C on a heated stir plate.
Stir gently until gelatin goes into solution; avoid introducing bubbles into the solution. The solution will be clear when gelatin is dissolved.
Once the gelatin is fully dissolved, add the Chromium Potassium Sulfate. Stir until dissolved.
Reduce heat and cool gelatin to ~50C prior to dipping slides. Slides should be coated immediately.
Unused solution can be diluted ≥2X with warm water and poured down the municipal drain.
Rinse the containers thoroughly with hot water then clean appropriately with MilliQ water and 70% EtOH.
